capabilities: detect whether the vault sits in a folder the device's cloud can sync
compare vaults across devices using beacon files and file fingerprints
resolve conflicted duplicate files with keep-newest or merge actions
flag iCloud-offloaded placeholder files as not downloaded
two-way sync the vault to GitHub on a schedule with a personal access token
disambiguation: Not a sync transport for iCloud or Google Drive; it only checks and repairs cloud sync setup — the optional GitHub mode is the only part that actually moves files.
extras: Makes no network requests at all unless GitHub storage is enabled (the only host contacted is api.github.com); installs via manual download or BRAT rather than a build toolchain. The manifest notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
problem: Cloud sync setups fail silently in ways Obsidian cannot see — a vault in the wrong folder, offloaded placeholder files, or duplicate conflict copies — with no way to verify or repair them.

relations.evidence: If you have the BRAT plugin, add jamalbalya/jemzsync and it will install and auto-update for you.
Obsidian Sync — official, paid, built for this, with version history.
Remotely Save — free community plugin supporting S3, Dropbox, OneDrive, WebDAV, with end-to-end encryption.
Working Copy — Git-based, good if you want full version control.

summary: Sync checker that verifies a vault sits where iCloud or Google Drive can reach it, compares devices via vault fingerprints, and resolves conflicted duplicates.
